Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Clinical concern for lateral meniscus tear.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.
Trace edema adjacent to the distal IT band.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. There is lateral patellar tilt and translation. Patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Increased tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 18 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Findings of active lateral patellar maltracking.
2.	Trace edema adjacent to distal IT band which could be related to friction.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: There is mild to moderate cartilage thinning and fissuring most prominent at the posterior weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: There is mild to moderate cartilage thinning and surface irregularity, most prominent at the posterior weightbearing aspect.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is a full-thickness cartilage delamination defect at the inferior aspect of the lateral patellar facet, measuring 1.0 cm in diameter. Cartilage delamination and flap formation is also noted at the lateral and central trochlea, measuring approximately 1.7 cm in diameter.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 8 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Tricompartmental chondrosis, most prominent in the patellofemoral compartment with areas of full-thickness cartilage delamination and flap formation.

2. Small joint effusion. Small Baker cyst.

MRI  KNEE  -  RIGHT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  locked knee - incarcerated meniscal tear.

COMPARISON:  Knee radiograph dated [Date]..

FINDINGS:

Medial meniscus:  Obliquely oriented undersurface tear along the posterior medial meniscus, measuring 2 mm in length.

Medial compartment articular cartilage:  Intact.

MCL:  Intact.

Lateral meniscus:  There is a displaced, full-thickness tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. The inner meniscal fragment is flipped centrally into the intercondylar notch and another component seen adjacent to the anterior horn.

Lateral compartment articular cartilage:  Focal blistering and intracartilaginous low-signal intensity area with an intact surface and bottom (201:15).

LCL complex:  Intact.

ACL:  Intact.

PCL:  Intact.

Quadriceps and patellar tendons:  Intact.

Patellofemoral alignment:  Normal. 

Patellofemoral cartilage:  Intact.

Joint effusion:  Small volume joint effusion.

Intra-articular bodies:  None.

Bone marrow:  Normal.

Popliteal fossa:  Incidental finding of 2.4 cm Baker cyst.

Other findings:  None.


INTERPRETATION:
1. Bucket-handle tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus with meniscus fragment flipped anteriorly towards the anterior horn lateral meniscus and centrally into the intercondylar notch.

2. Small nondisplaced undersurface meniscus tear along the posterior horn of the medial meniscus.

Findings: Moderate knee effusion. There is degenerate tearing of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Normal lateral meniscus.  There is severe thinning and loss of the medial compartment articular cartilage with subchondral bony change and osteophyte formation.  Mild lateral compartment osteophyte formation is noted. The lateral compartment articular cartilage is preserved.  Mild - moderate thinning of the patellofemoral articular cartilage is noted but no underlying bony change.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  
Conclusion: Severe medial compartment OA with degenerate tearing of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. The lateral compartment articular cartilage is preserved. Mild patellofemoral degeneration noted. Normal cruciate ligaments.

Findings: There is a mild knee effusion. Mild myxoid degeneration of the body of medial meniscus is noted. No definite tear is identified. Normal lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is moderate thinning and fraying of the medial compartment articular cartilage with partial extrusion of the medial meniscus from the joint. The lateral compartment articular cartilage is preserved. Severe patellar ridge and lateral patellar facet articular cartilage degeneration and loss with mild underlying bony change. Marked lateral trochlear facet articular cartilage degeneration is also noted.  
Conclusion: No evidence of meniscal tearing. Moderate medial tibiofemoral and severe patellofemoral degenerate change as described

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colateral lateral dentro de límites normales. Engrosamiento secuelar del
componente superficial y profundo del complejo medial en su aspecto proximal con algunos
fragmentos óseos secuelares.
El menisco lateral impresiona de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios categóricos de
rotura.
Rotura compleja del cuerpo y cuerno posterior del menisco medial con moderada extrusión
meniscal y edema las partes blandas.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibiales y patelofemoral sin alteraciones significativas.
Mínimo derrame articular. No hay quistes poplíteos patológicos.
Leve engrosamiento con cambios entesopáticos de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital.
Tendón rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites
normales.
Impresión:
Rotura compleja del menisco medial con moderada extrusión meniscal y edema de las partes
blandas adyacentes.
Cambios que impresionan secuelares del componente superficial y profundo del complejo
ligamentario medial.
Mínimo derrame articular.
Cambios entesopáticos cuadricipitales distales.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain with walking up and down stairs.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion with lipomatous synovial hypertrophy in the suprapatellar recess. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Bucket-handle variant tear of the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with a large displaced flap fragment into the intercondylar notch.
Medial compartment cartilage: High grade partial thickness cartilage loss along the medial weightbearing surfaces with deep cartilage fissuring cartilaginous flap formation.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Mild cartilage thinning and heterogeneity.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full-thickness cartilage loss along the medial patella with subchondral cystic change. High-grade partial thickness cartilage loss along the central trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: Mild proximal tendinosis without tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Bucket-handle variant tear of the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with a large displaced flap fragment into the intercondylar notch.
2.	Tricompartmental chondrosis, worse in the patellofemoral and medial compartments.
3.	Moderate joint effusion with lipomatous synovial hypertrophy.
4.	Mild distal quadriceps and proximal patellar tendinosis without tearing.

There is normal knee joint alignment.   Minimal superficial soft tissue and subcutaneous tissue stranding at the posterolateral aspect of the knee, along the biceps femoris myotendinous junction is noted.  
 No osteocartilagenous lesion is detected.  
 No focal bone marrow edema is noted.  
 Minimal amount of joint effusion is seen.  
  
 MCL is intact.    Medial meniscus is not torn.  
 FCL, popliteus and biceps femoris tendons are preserved.   
 Normal shape with preserved signal of the lateral meniscus is observed.   
  
 Normal course with preserved signal of the ACL is noted.  The PCL is intact.  
 PF joint surface is preserved.   No subchondral bone lesion is noted.  
 Quadriceps and patellar tendons are preserved.   Minimal superficial soft tissue edema at the posterolateral aspect of the knee,  
    along the biceps femoris myotendinous junction  
    No definite cartilagenous lesion. 
    No definite ligamentous tear. 
    No definite meniscal tear.

Findings: There is a mild - moderate knee effusion.  There is severe loss of the medial compartment articular cartilage. There is tearing of the posterior root of the medial meniscus with evidence of extrusion of the degenerate medial meniscus from the joint.  
The lateral compartment articular cartilage is preserved. Normal lateral meniscus.  Moderate - severe thinning of the patellar articular cartilage is noted, more so laterally. The trochlear articular cartilage is preserved.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. A loculated ganglion is noted just anterior to the gracilis tendon at the level of the posterior medial femoral condyle.  
Conclusion: Severe medial compartment degeneration with degenerate tearing and extrusion of the medial meniscus. Moderate lateral patellofemoral degeneration.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Dolor rodilla. Insuficiencia.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colateral lateral sin alteraciones. Leve engrosamiento secuelar del
componente superficial del ligamento colateral medial.
Rotura de predominio marginal del cuerpo y cuerno posterior del menisco lateral.
Rotura periférica del cuerno posterior y cuerpo del menisco medial que contacta la superficie
articular inferior con discreto edema las partes blandas adyacentes. No hay desplazamiento de
segmentos.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral
medial. El resto de los cartílagos femorotibiales sin alteraciones. Úlceras condrales focales de
espesor total de la tróclea femoral de predominio su región central así como también en la faceta
lateral y medial de la rótula, con cambios óseos secundarios.
Leve derrame articular. Pequeño quiste poplíteo con probable filtración.
Leve aumento de señal de la región insercional distal del tendón cuadricipital y proximal del
tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura.
Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Rotura de predominio marginal del menisco lateral.
Rotura periférica del menisco medial.
Leve engrosamiento secuelar del componente superficial del ligamento colateral medial.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial.
Condropatía lesiones grado 3 y 4 de la articulación patelofemoral.
Leve derrame articular. Pequeño quiste poplíteo con probable filtración.
Leve tendinosis cuadricipital distal y rotuliana proximal
